name: Multi-factor authentication
description: Require MFA for privileged accounts and sensitive operations to reduce identity spoofing.
implementation: Enforce MFA through the identity provider and prefer phishing-resistant factors when available.

name: Secure session management
description: Protect the session lifecycle against theft, fixation, and unauthorized reuse.
implementation: Use HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite cookies, rotate the session after login, and enforce expiration and invalidation.

name: Anti-abuse protections and rate limiting
description: Limit automated attempts and requests at entry points, especially login and account recovery.
implementation: Apply limits per user or source, progressive lockouts, timeouts, and request-size limits.
references: OWASP Credential Stuffing Prevention Cheat Sheet

name: Deny by default
description: Every operation must verify that the subject is authorized for the specific resource; anything not explicitly allowed is denied.
implementation: Enforce server-side authorization for every sensitive operation and verify access to the specific resource.

name: Least privilege
description: Users, services, and technical accounts receive only the permissions required for their role.
implementation: Assign minimal permissions by default, separate technical accounts, and review permissions periodically.

name: Separation of duties
description: Prevent a single identity from completing critical actions end to end without independent control.
implementation: Separate administrative duties and require additional approval for high-impact actions.

name: End-to-end TLS
description: Encrypt external and internal communications with correctly configured TLS and validate certificates.
implementation: Use HTTPS/TLS, validate certificates, and disable obsolete protocols or configurations.
references: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

name: mTLS between services
description: Mutually authenticate services with certificates when justified by the risk and architecture.
implementation: Use client and server certificates, automate their rotation, and reject unverifiable identities.
references: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

name: Message integrity and schema validation
description: Validate the structure and integrity of messages exchanged between components.
implementation: Validate messages against a known schema and use signatures or HMAC when integrity must be guaranteed.

name: Structured and correlated logging
description: Record relevant events with enough context to reconstruct who did what and when.
implementation: Log identity, action, resource, result, and timestamp, and propagate correlation identifiers.

name: Log data hygiene
description: Avoid unnecessary secrets and personal data in logs, applying masking where appropriate.
implementation: Do not log passwords, tokens, or authorization headers, and mask sensitive data that must be recorded.

name: Centralization, integrity, and alerting
description: Centralize logs, protect them against tampering, and generate alerts for relevant security events.
implementation: Send logs to a central system with restricted access, protect their integrity, and define alerting and retention policies.

name: Centralized secrets manager
description: Store keys, tokens, and passwords in a secrets manager instead of source code, images, or distributed files.
implementation: Use a central secrets manager as the single source of secrets and restrict access according to service identity.

name: Short-lived credentials and rotation
description: Reduce credential lifetime and automate rotation whenever possible.
implementation: Prefer temporary credentials, automate rotation, and maintain a revocation procedure.

name: Secure runtime secret injection
description: Provide secrets to processes at runtime without unnecessarily persisting or exposing them.
implementation: Inject secrets at runtime and avoid including them in repositories, images, command arguments, or logs.
